newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria updates bourse to service mass sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria updates bourse to service mass sell-offs.

text.p: Bulgaria has started modernising one of its stock exchanges with French help to prepare it to trade shares in newly-privatised companies next year, the head of the Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) board said on Thursday.

"The first phase -- an expert study of the specific conditions -- will be concluded at the end of this month after the experts' report is approved by the board," Viktor Papazov told a news conference.
By the end of December a detailed performance project will be worked out, and then new equipment and software will be installed, he said.
An agreement to modernise the BSE was signed on May 28 under an intergovernmental protocol on cooperation between Bulgaria and France.
The financing of the three phases of the project totals 2.5 million French francs, to be provided by the French government.

The Bulgarian government has launched a mass privatisation of state enterprises by issuing vouchers to Bulgarian adults which will be exchanged for shares. The first auctions were set for October 7 but have been postponed.

"A modern stock exchange is necessary as small investors -- who form the real stockmarket -- need a proper marketplace," said project manager Paul-Francois Dubroeuq, of the international relations and development department of the Paris Stock Exchange.

He said a clearing and settlement system needed to be established by Bulgaria's newly set up Central Depositary and the Securities and Stock Exchange Commission should make an effort to establish market regulations.
"Small investors' confidence in corporate paper has to be restored. That's why the Commission has to provide transparency on the companies traded on the bourses," said Dubroeuq.
Apart from the BSE another bourse, the Sofia Stock Exchange operates in Bulgaria. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
